title: Renormalized Macro-Cell / Substitution Automata
novelty_claim: Use cellular automata only in a certificate-first way: a finite macro-cell interface grammar should compose directly into exact legal `(X; d_i; f_i; T; R)` certificates, so the novelty is in scale-to-scale certificate transfer rather than in relabeling forcing as a CA.
closest_prior_art: Recursive product / tensor-power gadget families in arithmetic Kakeya small-graph constructions
differentiation: This survives prior-art pressure only if boundary interface types are pre-registered, exact-extractable, and predictive of score improvement across levels; otherwise it collapses into a dressed-up tensor product or a search prior with bespoke repair.
easiest_falsifier: Freeze one interface grammar and compare level-1 against level-2 exact extractions. If interface overhead grows as fast as solved volume, or exact extraction needs scale-specific global repair, reject the direction immediately.
evidence_plan: Freeze a finite macro-cell interface alphabet and an exact extractor to legal `(X; d_i; f_i; T; R)` data.
Test level-to-level transfer on anisotropic recursive products with low-height asymmetric `X`, measuring extracted `(m+r)/(n-t)` rather than proxy dynamics.
Benchmark against direct no-CA certificate search on the same geometry and abandon unless transfer improves under stage-order and aspect-ratio perturbations.

budget_envelope.compute: None until interface grammar, baseline matrix, and symmetry quotients are frozen
budget_envelope.search_scope: One narrow motif family, level-1 and level-2 only

title: Target-Direction Abelian-Network Forcing
novelty_claim: Import abelian-network or Smith-normal-form invariants only as a narrow screening signal for exact arithmetic Kakeya certificates, with the specific claim that target-direction structure can predict low-score forcing better than plain arithmetic descriptors.
closest_prior_art: Abelian networks I-III and chip-firing / sandpile critical-group literature
Green-Ruzsa and Katz-Tao style arithmetic forcing frameworks
differentiation: The claim must stay weaker than 'arithmetic Kakeya forcing is an abelian network'. It is only differentiated if target-direction invariants add predictive power after exact extraction and after matching on raw relation-matrix features, `|X|`, coordinate height, and geometry.
easiest_falsifier: On matched exact-extracted families, compare invariant-guided screening against direct arithmetic features such as rank, determinant pattern, support size, and edge density. If the imported invariants do not improve prediction or score frontier, drop the bridge.
evidence_plan: Define the target-direction invariant package only on exact-extracted candidate families.
Run a matched predictive comparison against direct arithmetic features on the same geometries and low-height asymmetric `X` choices.
Continue only if the invariant screen retains nearly all best exact certificates while discarding a substantial fraction of weak controls.

title: Slope-Bloom Spacetime Automata
novelty_claim: A fixed small local CA rule might realize growing effective slope or rational complexity under exact extraction, giving a genuinely CA-native way to escape the bounded-slope basin without manually enlarging `X`.
closest_prior_art: Bounded-slope and rational-complexity arithmetic Kakeya work
differentiation: This is only distinct if the extracted label complexity genuinely grows with scale. If unrolling produces periodic or bounded effective slope sets, it is just another bounded-slope retuning story.
easiest_falsifier: Exact-extract a few scales from one fixed rule. If realized slope complexity stays `O(1)` or quickly becomes periodic, reject the direction as trapped in the explored bounded-slope regime.
evidence_plan: Freeze a very small rule class and an exact unrolling-to-certificate extractor before any search.
Measure effective realized slope and rational complexity under scale, not fill-time or occupancy proxies.
Abandon unless extracted score trends beat matched bounded-slope controls and direct `X`-generator baselines.
